items.en: Can I have a coffee, please?
items.note: Politer than 我要一杯咖啡, the usual way to order. Add 謝謝 once you get it
items.mission: Order your next coffee on campus with 可以給我一杯咖啡嗎？
items.situation: You're at the counter of a café and want a coffee.

items.zh: 可以用英文解釋一下嗎？
items.pinyin: kě-yǐ yòng Yīng-wén jiě-shì yī-xià ma?
items.en: Can you explain this in English?
items.note: The longer version of 可以說英文嗎？ 用英文 = using English, before the verb. 解釋 = to explain; 一下 softens it
items.mission: When a colleague or your coach says something you can't follow, ask 可以用英文解釋一下嗎？
items.situation: Someone explains something in Chinese and you're lost.

items.note: Becomes bú before a 4th tone: 不要 bú yào, 不是 bú shì
Put at the end of a statement to make a yes/no question
yī when counting; yí before a 4th tone, yì before tones 1–3 (一點點 yì diǎndiǎn)
二 èr for counting and numbers; 兩 liǎng for two of something
兩 liǎng for amounts: two cups, two people; 二 èr for counting
回家 huí jiā = go home
Negate with 沒 (méi), not 不: 沒有 méi yǒu
Also marks an ongoing action: 我在學中文 = I'm learning Chinese
jiāo as a verb; jiào in 教授 (professor)
知道 = know a fact; 認識 = know a person
Don't confuse with 賣 mài (to sell)

items.en: to want to; to think; to miss
items.note: 想 is softer than 要: 我想喝… = I'd like to drink…
會說中文 = can speak Chinese (have learned to)

Rice porridge

items.situation: You greet a group of students.
items.mission: Greet a group with 你們好
items.note: 們 men makes a plural: 你們 = you (all), 我們 = we. For greeting a group, 大家好 is more common

items.situation: Someone asks how you are.
Someone asks how you are; ask back.

items.note: 有沒有 = have or not have: a yes/no question without 嗎

items.en: I don't eat spicy food (in general)
items.situation: The waiter asks if you want chilli; you never eat it.
items.note: 不 = don't (in general, habits). 沒 = didn't / haven't (it didn't happen)

items.situation: Someone asks if your lunch was spicy. It wasn't.
items.note: 沒 = didn't / haven't. Compare 我不吃辣: I don't eat spicy food

items.situation: You start telling a colleague what happened at lunch yesterday.
items.note: … 的時候 = at the time of …, when …

items.situation: You want a colleague's opinion.
items.mission: Ask someone's opinion with 你覺得怎麼樣？
items.note: 覺得 = to feel / think (your own opinion)

items.situation: Someone asks if you had your coffee. You did.
items.note: 了 le after a verb: the action happened

items.situation: You want to check if someone knows something.
items.note: Verb 不 verb makes a yes/no question: 知不知道, 可不可以, 有沒有

items.situation: You want to ask if something is allowed.
items.mission: Ask 可不可以？ before taking a free seat

items.pinyin: zhè-ge rén shì wǒ de nǚ-péng-yǒu
items.situation: You introduce your girlfriend to someone.
items.note: A grammar example: 我的 = my, 這個人 = this person. When you introduce her, say 這是我女朋友

items.situation: You've answered one question and check for more.
items.mission: End a class or meeting with 有沒有其他問題？

items.en: Do you have any other times for class?

items.mission: Ask your coach about another lesson time in Mandarin
items.note: 時間 = time (in general, a slot). 時候 = a moment (… 的時候 = when …)

items.situation: Your weekly lesson is ending.
items.mission: Say 下星期見！ at the end of your lesson

items.situation: You say it's your first time doing something.
items.note: 第一 = first (the usual word). 首 = first in formal contexts (首次)

items.note: 杯 bēi is the measure word for cups: 一杯咖啡

items.note: 過 guò after a verb: you have done it (at some point)

items.situation: You leave and will see them {day}.

items.note: 首 in formal contexts (首次 = the first time); everyday: 第一
以前 = in the past (general). 之前 = before (a specific moment)
以後 = in the future (general). 之後 = after (a specific moment)
… 的時候 = when … / at the time of …
Taiwan: xīngqí; mainland: xīngqī
The most common measure word: 一個人, 這個
穿 wear + 搭 match: the everyday Taiwan word for an outfit (how the clothes go together). 我喜歡你的穿搭 = I like your outfit
items.mission: Compliment a friend's outfit: 我喜歡你的穿搭
items.situation: You want to name what someone is wearing today, as a whole look.

items.note: 我很好 + 你呢？ said in one breath. 呢 bounces the same question back, so you don't have to repeat 你好嗎
items.mission: Next time a colleague at CUHK asks 你好嗎？ or 最近怎麼樣？, answer 我很好，你呢？
items.situation: Someone asks how you are and you want to return the question.

items.note: 普通話 is what Mandarin is called in Hong Kong, where 中文 usually means Cantonese. In Taiwan people say 中文 or 國語 (guóyǔ), so with your coach 我在學中文 is enough
items.mission: Tell someone in Hong Kong that it's Mandarin you're learning: 我在學普通話
items.situation: Someone in Hong Kong asks whether you're learning Cantonese or Mandarin.

items.pinyin: zhè jù huà Zhōng-wén zěn-me shuō?
items.en: How do I say this (sentence) in Chinese?
items.note: 這句話 = this sentence (句 counts sentences). The short version does the same job: 這個中文怎麼說？
items.mission: In your next lesson, say something in English and ask your coach 這句話中文怎麼說？
items.situation: You know what you want to say in English but not in Chinese.

items.pinyin: wǒ shì cóng Hé-lán lái de
items.note: 是…的 wraps the detail you're stressing (where from). 從 cóng = from, 來 = come. 我是荷蘭人 says the same in fewer words
items.mission: When a student or taxi driver asks 你是哪裡人？, answer 我是從荷蘭來的
items.situation: Someone asks where you're from.

items.note: The everyday Taiwan reply to 謝謝, lighter than 不客氣. When someone asks a favour, the answer is 沒問題
items.mission: When a student thanks you after class, answer 不會！
items.situation: Someone thanks you for a small favour.
You walk into a shop or meet someone.
items.mission: Greet the staff with 你好 the next time you walk into a shop

items.situation: You point at something on the menu.
items.mission: Order by pointing at the menu: 我要這個
items.note: The normal way to order: direct, not rude. 可以給我這個嗎？ is the politer version

items.situation: You need to get past someone or catch a waiter's attention.
items.mission: Use 不好意思 to get a waiter's attention or to squeeze past someone on the MTR
items.note: The all-purpose "excuse me": getting attention, squeezing past, a small slip. 對不起 is for a real apology

items.situation: You are late or made a real mistake.
items.mission: Apologise with 對不起 the next time you're late
items.note: A real apology. For small things (bumping into someone, interrupting), 不好意思 is more usual

items.situation: Someone apologises to you.
items.mission: Answer 沒關係 when someone says sorry to you

items.situation: Someone suggests something and you agree.
items.mission: Agree to a plan with 好的
items.note: Just 好 works too. With friends: 好啊 (hǎo a) = sure!

items.situation: Someone checks a fact with you and they are right.
items.mission: Confirm something with 對 instead of nodding
items.note: Chinese has no single word for yes. 對 confirms what someone said; otherwise repeat the verb (你是老師嗎？ 是)

items.situation: A waiter offers you a bag or more tea and you don't want it.
items.mission: Turn down a plastic bag with 不用，謝謝

items.situation: You need a moment before answering or ordering.
items.mission: Ask for a moment with 等一下 while you read the menu

items.situation: You want to know the price of something.
items.mission: Ask 多少錢？ at a market stall

items.situation: You've finished eating and want to pay.
items.mission: Ask for the bill with 買單
items.note: Understood in Hong Kong too (Cantonese: maai4 daan1). Add 謝謝 after it

items.situation: You are about to ask a stranger a question.
items.mission: Start a question to a stranger with 請問
items.note: Goes in front of any question to a stranger: 請問，多少錢？

items.situation: You are leaving.
items.mission: Say 再見 when you leave your lesson
items.note: Friends mostly say 掰掰 (bāi-bāi, bye-bye)

items.situation: You introduce your girlfriend to a colleague.
items.mission: Introduce your girlfriend to someone: 這是我女朋友
items.note: With family and partners 的 is usually dropped: 我女朋友, 我媽媽

items.situation: You're waiting for someone who is still packing up.
items.mission: Ask a colleague who is packing up after a meeting: 好了嗎？
items.note: 好了 = done, ready (了 marks the change). Yes: 好了. Not yet: 還沒

items.situation: Someone asks 好了嗎？ and you need more time.
items.mission: When someone asks whether you're ready or have eaten, answer 還沒呢
items.note: 還沒 alone is enough; 呢 makes it sound relaxed, "not yet, you know"

items.situation: You've said something and want the other person to confirm.
items.mission: End a sentence with 對不對？ to check you got something right with your coach
items.note: Tag question after a statement. Answer: 對 (right) or 不對 (not right)

items.situation: You've suggested a plan and ask whether it suits them.
items.mission: Suggest coffee and add 好不好？: 我們去喝咖啡，好不好？
items.note: Goes after a suggestion. Answer: 好 (OK) or 不好 (no)

items.situation: Someone thanks you warmly.
items.mission: Answer 不客氣 when someone thanks you for holding the door
items.note: The standard reply to 謝謝, understood everywhere. In Taiwan, 不會 is the lighter everyday one

items.en: Can you say it in English?
items.situation: Someone explains something in Chinese and you're lost.
items.mission: When you can't follow your coach or a colleague, ask 可以說英文嗎？
